## Reviewer's Guide

This PR adds a Terraform layer that provisions the AWS network, security boundary, EC2 host, SSH key registration, and Elastic IP, then wires Terraform output into Ansible through Makefile automation so the host is configured using freshly generated inventory. Documentation is updated to describe the combined workflow and state-management model, while the obsolete root vault is removed. Validation was performed with Terraform formatting/validation and Ansible syntax/lint checks; no Terraform apply was run.

#### Sequence diagram for Terraform and Ansible deployment

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant User
    participant Make
    participant Terraform
    participant Inventory
    participant Ansible
    participant EC2
    User->>Make: make up
    Make->>Terraform: init
    Make->>Terraform: apply -auto-approve
    Terraform-->>Make: instance_public_ip
    Make->>Inventory: terraform output -raw instance_public_ip
    Inventory-->>Make: write inventory.yaml
    Make->>Ansible: ansible-playbook site.yml
    Ansible->>EC2: configure host using ansible_host
```

#### Flow diagram for Elastic IP inventory synchronization

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Apply[terraform apply] --> EIP[Elastic IP attached to EC2]
    EIP --> Output[terraform output -raw instance_public_ip]
    Output --> Inventory[make inventory rewrites inventory.yaml]
    Inventory --> Ansible[Ansible targets current EC2 address]
```

### File-Level Changes

| Change | Details | Files |
| ------ | ------- | ----- |
| Add Terraform-managed AWS infrastructure for the Ansible-configured WordPress host. | <ul><li>Define the AWS provider, region, AMI lookup, and configurable instance/network inputs.</li><li>Create a VPC, public subnet, internet gateway, default route, and route-table association.</li><li>Restrict inbound traffic to SSH, HTTP, and HTTPS, with unrestricted outbound access.</li><li>Provision the EC2 instance with an encrypted gp3 root volume and an SSH key derived from the existing private key.</li><li>Attach an Elastic IP and expose it through a Terraform output.</li></ul> | `terraform/main.tf`<br/>`terraform/outputs.tf`<br/>`terraform/variables.tf`<br/>`terraform/versions.tf` |
| Connect infrastructure provisioning to host configuration through Make targets and generated inventory. | <ul><li>Derive the public SSH key, initialize/apply Terraform, regenerate inventory from the Elastic IP output, and run the Ansible playbook via `make up`.</li><li>Add dry-run, lint/validation, formatting, and destroy workflows.</li><li>Document the Terraform/Ansible division, infrastructure layout, Elastic IP rationale, and operational commands.</li></ul> | `Makefile`<br/>`README.md` |
| Remove obsolete repository secrets and update ignore configuration. | <ul><li>Delete the unused, unreadable week-one root-level vault file.</li><li>Retain the active group-vars vault as the documented secrets source.</li><li>Update ignored files for the Terraform workflow.</li></ul> | `vault.yml`<br/>`.gitignore` |

  (re-)generate the summary at any time.

  pull request to resolve all Sourcery comments. Useful if you've already
  addressed all the comments and don't want to see them anymore.
- **Dismiss all Sourcery reviews:** Comment `@sourcery-ai dismiss` on the pull
  request to dismiss all existing Sourcery reviews. Especially useful if you
  want to start fresh with a new review - don't forget to comment
  `@sourcery-ai review` to trigger a new review!

<details open><summary><h3>Greptile Summary</h3></summary>

The PR adds Terraform-managed AWS networking, compute, SSH key, and Elastic IP resources, plus Make targets that provision infrastructure, regenerate Ansible inventory, and configure the host.

- Creates a public VPC subnet with internet routing and ingress limited to SSH, HTTP, and HTTPS.
- Provisions an Ubuntu EC2 instance with encrypted storage and an attached Elastic IP.
- Connects Terraform output to the existing Ansible deployment workflow.
- Updates documentation and ignores generated Terraform and SSH-key artifacts.
</details>


<details open><summary><h3>Confidence Score: 4/5</h3></summary>

The PR needs an instance-readiness step before merging because a first-run `make up` can reach Ansible before the new host accepts SSH connections.

The infrastructure definitions are internally consistent, but the advertised end-to-end workflow crosses the Terraform-to-Ansible lifecycle boundary without checking guest readiness, making fresh deployments timing-dependent.

**Files Needing Attention:** Makefile
</details>


<details open><summary><h3>Important Files Changed</h3></summary>




| Filename | Overview |
|----------|----------|
| Makefile | Adds the end-to-end Terraform and Ansible workflow, but does not wait for a newly created instance to become SSH-ready before configuration. |
| terraform/main.tf | Defines the public AWS network, constrained security group, EC2 instance, key pair, encrypted root volume, and Elastic IP. |
| terraform/variables.tf | Provides region, instance size, key path, SSH source CIDR, and network CIDR defaults. |
| terraform/outputs.tf | Exposes the Elastic IP consumed by inventory generation and the selected Ubuntu AMI. |
| terraform/versions.tf | Constrains Terraform and AWS provider versions and configures regional provider defaults. |
| README.md | Documents the Terraform architecture, Make workflow, Elastic IP rationale, and Terraform-versus-Ansible ownership model. |

</details>

Hey - I've found 1 security issue, and 3 other issues

**Security issues**:
- Ensure Instance Metadata Service Version 1 is not enabled ([link](https://github.com/yel-hadr/cloud-1_42/pull/2/files#diff-2e617c7870fa918457b1eee1c7d67ba82f19d043ae7b7918db26873e18793028R117-131))

<details>
<summary>Prompt for AI Agents</summary>

~~~markdown
Please address the comments from this code review:

## Individual Comments

### Comment 1
<location path="Makefile" line_range="41" />
<code_context>
+
+lint:
+	ansible-lint
+	$(TF) fmt -check -recursive
+	$(TF) validate
+
</code_context>
<issue_to_address>
**issue (bug_risk):** `make lint` fails on a fresh checkout because `terraform validate` requires the Terraform working directory to be initialized, while this target never runs `terraform init`. The `.terraform/` directory is ignored, so it is absent unless `make provision` was run first.

**Triggers:** When `make lint` is run before `make up` or `make provision` on a clean checkout.

**Suggested fix:** Run `$(TF) init -backend=false -input=false` before `$(TF) validate`, or make `lint` depend on an initialization target.

```suggestion
	$(TF) init -backend=false -input=false
	$(TF) validate
```
</issue_to_address>

### Comment 2
<location path="Makefile" line_range="12" />
<code_context>
+
+.PHONY: up down provision inventory configure check lint fmt destroy-check
+
+up: provision inventory configure
+
+# Terraform reads the public half; ansible.cfg connects with the private
</code_context>
<issue_to_address>
**issue (bug_risk):** `make up` starts `ansible-playbook` immediately after `terraform apply` returns, without waiting for the newly created Ubuntu instance to accept SSH. Terraform waits for the EC2 resource state, not for cloud-init, sshd, or the initial OS boot to finish, so the first configuration step fails with an unreachable-host error when SSH is not ready.

**Triggers:** When `make up` creates a new instance and Ansible connects before the instance finishes booting.

**Suggested fix:** Add an explicit SSH readiness wait/retry between `provision` and `configure`, such as an Ansible `wait_for_connection` task or a Makefile retry loop.

```suggestion
up: provision
	$(MAKE) inventory
	@until ansible all -i inventory.yaml -m ansible.builtin.wait_for_connection; do sleep 5; done
	$(MAKE) configure
```
</issue_to_address>

### Comment 3
<location path="Makefile" line_range="27-32" />
<code_context>
+# the instance that actually exists rather than a stale hard-coded address.
+inventory:
+	@IP=$$($(TF) output -raw instance_public_ip) && \
+	printf -- '---\n# Generated by `make inventory` from terraform output.\nwebservers:\n  hosts:\n    cloud1:\n      ansible_host: %s\n' "$$IP" > inventory.yaml && \
+	echo "inventory.yaml -> $$IP"
+
+configure:
+	ansible-galaxy collection install -r requirements.yml
+	ansible-playbook site.yml
+
+# Dry run. Always worth doing before touching a working box.
</code_context>
<issue_to_address>
**issue (broader_impact):** The end-to-end target rewrites `ansible_host` to the newly allocated EIP but never updates or verifies the DNS A records used by the Let's Encrypt preflight. On a first apply, the new EIP is different from the address currently published in DNS, so `configure` brings up the stack and then aborts during certificate setup with the stale-DNS assertion.

**Triggers:** When the Terraform state is empty or the instance is rebuilt behind a newly allocated EIP while DNS still points at the old address.

**Suggested fix:** Manage the DNS records in Terraform or make `up` wait for/require the DNS records to be updated before running the TLS-enabled playbook.
</issue_to_address>

### Comment 4
<location path="terraform/main.tf" line_range="117-131" />
<code_context>

</code_context>
<issue_to_address>
**security (CKV_AWS_79):** Ensure Instance Metadata Service Version 1 is not enabled

The Instance Metadata Service (IMDS) is an on-instance component used by code on the instance to securely access instance metadata.

You can access instance metadata from a running instance using one of the following methods:

* Instance Metadata Service Version 1 (IMDSv1) -- a request/response method
* Instance Metadata Service Version 2 (IMDSv2) -- a session-oriented method

As a request/response method IMDSv1 is prone to local misconfigurations:

* Open proxies, open NATs and routers, server-side reflection vulnerabilities.
* One way or another, local software might access local-only data.

<details>
<summary>Fix</summary>

*Terraform*


* *Resource:* aws_instance
* *Arguments:* http_tokens - (Optional) Whether or not the metadata service requires session tokens, the mechanism used for Instance Metadata  Service Version 2.

Can be "optional" or "required".
(Default: "optional").
*Set to "required" to enable Instance Metadata Service V2.*
Alternatively, disable the metadata service altogether by setting `http_endpoint = "disabled"`.


```go
resource "aws_instance" "example" {
  ...
  instance_type     = "t2.micro"
+   metadata_options {
        ...
+       http_endpoint = "enabled"
+       http_tokens   = "required"
+  }
  ...
}
```

If setting `http_tokens = "required"` in a launch template that is being used for a EKS worker/node group, you should consider setting the `http_put_response_hop_limit = 2` per the https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2020/08/amazon-eks-supports-ec2-instance-metadata-service-v2/[default behavior in EKS].
Without this setting the default service account in EKS will not be able to access the instance metadata service.


*CloudFormation*


* *Resource:* AWS::EC2::LaunchTemplate
* *Arguments:* Properties.MetadataOptions.HttpEndpoint /  Properties.MetadataOptions.HttpTokens


```yaml
Resources:
  IMDSv1Disabled:
    Type: AWS::EC2::LaunchTemplate
    Properties:
        ...
      LaunchTemplateData:
        ...
+       MetadataOptions:
+         HttpEndpoint: disabled

  IMDSv2Enabled:
    Type: AWS::EC2::LaunchTemplate
    Properties:
      ...
      LaunchTemplateData:
        ...
+       MetadataOptions:
+         HttpTokens: required
```

</details>

*Source: checkov*
</issue_to_address>
~~~

</details>
